label: Reduction in One Picture
notes: Open by framing reduction as a two-step repair. Restricting omega to the zero level introduces null directions; the quotient by the group then removes exactly those directions. Stress that the orbit directions and the null directions coincide, which is the whole engine of the proof we will unpack today.

label: The Setup
notes: Recall the data: a symplectic manifold, a compact Lie group acting in a Hamiltonian way, and a moment map into the dual Lie algebra. Emphasize compactness or properness guarantees the quotient is Hausdorff. Everything downstream rests on two hypotheses about the zero level that we isolate next.

label: Statement of the Theorem
notes: State Marsden-Weinstein-Meyer precisely. Two hypotheses: zero is a regular value and the action on the level set is free. Conclusion: the reduced space is a smooth symplectic manifold whose dimension drops by twice the group dimension. Point at the dimension formula and promise to explain every clause.

label: Why Zero Is Regular
notes: Explain the moment-map differential. The image of d-mu at a point is the annihilator of the stabilizer algebra. Freeness kills the stabilizer, so the differential is surjective and zero is regular. This makes the level set a submanifold of codimension equal to the group dimension.

label: The Coisotropic Level Set
notes: Derive the key identity: the kernel of d-mu equals the symplectic orthogonal of the orbit tangent space. Because the orbit is isotropic, its orthogonal contains it, so the level set is coisotropic. The orbit directions sit inside the level set as the null directions of the restricted form.

label: The Linear Lemma
notes: Do the pure linear algebra first. Given an isotropic subspace of a symplectic vector space, the form descends to the quotient of its orthogonal by itself, and is nondegenerate there. This is the tangent-space model for the reduced space, and it is where nondegeneracy is actually proven.

label: Quotient by the Null Foliation
notes: Geometrize the lemma. The null directions of the restricted form foliate the level set, and the leaves are exactly the group orbits. Collapsing each orbit to a point gives the reduced space. The slice theorem supplies charts and makes the projection a principal bundle with fiber G.

label: The Reduced Symplectic Form
notes: Define omega-red by the pullback identity: i-star omega equals pi-star omega-red. Uniqueness follows because pi is a surjective submersion, so its pullback is injective on forms. Nondegeneracy is the linear lemma applied pointwise. This is the heart of the construction.

label: Closedness of omega-red
notes: Walk through the naturality chase. Pi-star of d-omega-red equals d of pi-star omega-red equals d of i-star omega equals i-star of d-omega, which is zero. Since pi-star is injective, d-omega-red vanishes. Closedness plus nondegeneracy means omega-red is genuinely symplectic.

label: Worked Model: C^2 by S^1
notes: Run the concrete model. The diagonal circle on C-two with the radius-squared moment map has the three-sphere as its zero level. Each circle orbit collapses to a point of complex projective one-space. The dimensions drop four to three to two, the smallest faithful picture of the whole theorem.

label: Descending Symmetries and Recap
notes: Close with the commuting-action remark: a second Hamiltonian action commuting with G, whose moment map is G-invariant, descends to the reduced space. Then recap the pipeline once more: cut to the level set, quotient by orbits, inherit the form. Preview staged and singular reduction for next time.
